newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq-backed Kurd guerrillas enter key Iraq city.
newsitem.headline: Iraq-backed Kurd guerrillas enter key Iraq city.

text.p: An Iraqi Kurdish militia aligned with Baghdad entered on Monday the main stronghold of its Kurdish rival in a lightning drive through northern Iraq, Iraqi Kurds and U.N. officials said.
The Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) of Massoud Barzani said its forces had met little resistance from Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) fighters as they pushed into the city of Sulaimaniya.
"The battle for Sulaimaniya is over. Massoud Barzani fighters have entered the city without fighting," a U.N. official told Reuters in Baghdad by telephone from Arbil.
The city, with a population of around a million, is the biggest Kurdish urban centre in Iraq and had long been the headquarters of Jalal Talabani's PUK.
There was no immediate comment from the PUK. U.N. officials said they did not know Talabani's whereabouts.

In Dukan, a town about 70 km (45 miles) away which the KDP seized earlier in the day, leading KDP member Dr Ross Nouri Shawis told reporters: "KDP troops entered Sulaimaniya from the direction of Halabja at 7 p.m. (1500 GMT). They were welcomed by the local population with flowers."

He said the only "serious resistance" along a 76-km (46-mile) route from Halabja near the Iranian border, east of Sulaimaniya, was at Sayed Sadeq, a major highway junction at the 50-km (30-mile) mark.

Shawis received word in a military dispatch delivered by hand. Earlier in the day KDP commander Massoud Barzani, leading his forces from Dukan north of Sulaimaniya, said he did not expect to move on the city on Monday.
U.N. sources said they could not give a figure on casualties or number of people displaced in the factional fighting.

The KDP seized the international spotlight on August 31 when, aided by Baghdad, the militia captured the Kurdish capital Arbil from the PUK. The United States retaliated against Saddam by firing 44 cruise missiles on southern Iraq.
The KDP says it has since fought its rivals without the help of the Iraqi government.
